title: Working Around Fans
summary: Unguarded fan blades within reach can cause serious injuries. This talk covers OSHA's rule on guarding fans within 7 feet of the floor or working level. The interpretation comes from the general-industry standard 29 CFR 1910.212(a)(5); the same 7 foot and one-half inch rule appears in the construction standard 29 CFR 1926.300(b)(2).
talking_points: All fans within 7 feet of the floor or working level must be guarded.
The guard must not have openings greater than one-half inch in width.
Concentric rings spaced no more than one-half inch apart are acceptable if there are enough radial spokes and firm mountings to keep the guard rigid.
The guard must be rigid enough that it cannot be pushed into the fan blade during normal use.

Nylon mesh or a similar material with holes no larger than one-half inch may be used to fix a substandard guard on an existing fan. The mesh and guard together must be strong enough that the mesh cannot be pushed into the blade.
Floor fans are a common case. Check them for missing or bent guards.
Report any fan with a missing or damaged guard so it is fixed.
site_hazards_to_check: Fans within 7 feet of the floor or working level with no guard
Guard openings wider than one-half inch
Guards that flex or can be pushed into the blade
Floor fans where the guard has been removed or damaged
discussion_questions: Which fans on our site are within 7 feet of the floor or working level?
How can you tell if a fan guard is rigid enough?
Who do you tell if you find a fan with no guard?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA Instruction STD 01-12-001, Defining Acceptable Guarding of Fan Blades. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: Every figure (7 ft, one-half inch openings, concentric rings, rigid, nylon mesh retrofit) is quote-accurate to OSHA Instruction STD 1-12.1 (1978). Point 6 (floor fans) reflects the background statement; point 7 (report a damaged guard) is practical advice not in the source.

FIX MADE: the talk cited only general-industry 1910.212(a)(5) and did not say so. Verified that 29 CFR 1926.300(b) carries the same fan rule (blades less than 7 ft above floor or working level guarded, openings no larger than 1/2 inch). Added 1926.300(b)(2) and a general-industry disclosure in the summary.
Non-blocking: the directive dates from 1978; fine as an interpretation but not a current construction directive. Public domain, osha.gov. No UK wording.
